payload.title: bundle-budget-adapter probes, reads and records vite.config.mts as a read path, but the manifest's allowed_read_globs cover only .ts, .tsx, .js and .json under web, so a module with a vite.config.mts would turn the whole run into a scope_violation.
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/bundle-budget-adapter.ts:240-248 (the probe list includes vite.config.mts and the found path is pushed to readPaths)
tools/aria-adapters/bundle-budget-adapter.ts:255-257 (the text of the found config is read and parsed)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tool_health.py:168-171 (a read path outside the allow list sets the run status to scope_violation)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tool_health.py:811-821 (a non-matching path becomes a violation once an allow list is declared)
payload.rule_violated: The adapter's declared read surface must cover what the adapter reads (manifest allowed_read_globs versus the probe list); ARIA-LOW-594 sets the same principle for declared_scope.
payload.notes: Adding web/modules/x/vite.config.mts (no config of that name exists at this revision) puts that path into read_paths, find_scope_violations reports it, and the whole bundle-budget run is recorded as scope_violation instead of emitting findings for every module. Close condition: Either remove vite.config.mts from the probe list or add web/**/*.mts to allowed_read_globs and declared_scope; add a kernel or adapter test that every config file name the adapter probes matches an allowed glob. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 3). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
